items.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 8 at 7:01AM PDT until September 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions
with high temperatures in the mid 80s at the beaches to 90s for
higher coastal terrain with low temperatures in the lower to mid
70s. For the Heat Advisory, high temperatures around 80 near the
coast to the lower to mid 90s for higher coastal terrain.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas and San Diego County Coastal
Areas.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT Wednesday. For
the Heat Advisory, from 8 PM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 8 at 2:29AM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 3 to 6 feet with sets up to 8
feet, highest at south and southwest-facing beaches. Strong and
dangerous rip and longshore currents. Minor coastal flooding
from a combination of high surf and high astronomical tides
during the evenings.

* WHERE...Beaches of Orange and San Diego Counties.

* WHEN...Through 11 PM PDT today.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Predicted higher high tides:
Newport Beach: 7.0 feet at 7:59 PM. La Jolla: 6.9 feet at 7:54 PM.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.
